Hi Aisha — thanks for the note and the heads-up on your timeline. We can absolutely support this. Quick summary of what Redwood can provide and typical constraints: 

- Report: a redacted SOC 2 Type II report for the audit period Oct 1, 2023 — Sep 30, 2024. We remove vendor pricing and a small set of internal-only identifiers; the control testing and auditor opinion remain intact. (Attachment: Redwood-SOC2-TypeII-2023-10_2024-09-redacted.pdf)
- Bridge letter: yes, we can provide a bridge letter that extends attestation coverage for the period between the report end date and a later contract start date. We include a draft template you can review. (Attachment: Redwood-Bridge-Letter-Template.docx)
- Questionnaire exports: we can share a CAIQ summary and a machine-readable SIG export for procurement review. We typically provide a CSV or ZIP export; see CAIQ-summary-2024.csv attached.

Sharing logistics and requirements:
- We prefer to share the report and bridge letter via an SSO-protected Google Drive folder (or Box) and can also route via a controlled DocuSign envelope if you need a signed acknowledgment. Drive link will expire in 14 days.
- No additional NDA is required for the redacted SOC 2 report; however, if you need the unredacted report or deeper artifact-level evidence, we require a standard mutual NDA and a specific evidence request list.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll upload the redacted report, bridge-letter draft, and CAIQ export to a secure folder and send a link by EOD.
2) If you confirm you need unredacted artifacts, please send a prioritized evidence list and we’ll route an NDA and an auditor-escorted access plan.
3) If you want us to sign a short acknowledgement via DocuSign, confirm the recipient email.

Tentative timeline: redacted report + CAIQ by today (EOD PDT); bridge-letter draft within 24 hours after you confirm desired language.

Sharing the link shortly — cc’ing Marissa and Vivek for visibility (Marissa handles audit packaging; Vivek handles compliance escalations).

Best,

Tessa Morgan

1) Will the CAIQ export include evidence-level links (the standard CAIQ mapping) or only the high-level answers? Our security team needs the mapping for tool comparison.
2) For the bridge letter, can you include language clarifying whether key management and logging controls remained in production without change after the report period? That helps our risk committee.

If you can confirm both items, we’ll mark the request as high priority and expect to review materials by 2026-09-10.

—Sam

2) Bridge letter language: we can include a statement that there were no material changes to KMS configuration and core logging pipelines between 2024-10-01 and the present, subject to a standard exception clause. Marissa will draft the final wording to satisfy your risk committee.
